verdicts.observed: Grid row membership is driven by the DEPARTMENT on the staff record, not by role. The 22 grid rows group under SERVICE/PARTS and SERVICE plus an UNASSIGNED lane, and they include an Admin-role person (MQ Test Tech No, departments Heavy Duty/Service and Heavy Duty/Service/Parts) who appears under BOTH department groups, plus job titles that are plainly not technicians - Parts Technician, Equipment Sales, Shop Labourer, Welder, Foreman. Conversely 10 active staff hold NO Heavy-Duty department and NONE of them appears as a row.
verdicts.limitation: 15 of the 17 named grid people have no staff record at all, so the department correlation could only be tested against the 2 who do. That absence is SV-8922 / SV-8921, not this case.

verdicts.observed: The sidebar never collapses and it is the PAGE that scrolls sideways, not the grid. documentElement.scrollWidth stays pinned at 1030 while the viewport narrows - measured at 1000, 960, 900 and 700px - and the sidebar holds 275px (outer 299px) at every one of them. No grid-level horizontal scroller exists at all: the only elements that overflow are HTML, BODY and the page containers. At 1680px there is no page overflow at all (scrollWidth == clientWidth == 1680). 0 errors at every width. This reproduces AT the supported 960px minimum, not merely below it, which is stronger than the case's existing note.

The sidebar list does not virtualize. With 91 work orders available it holds 18 cards in the DOM and offers a 'Load More' button. Scrolling it through five positions (0, 25, 50, 75, 100 percent of 2817px) is smooth and the DOM count stays at 18 with no blank stretches, so the smoothness half is fine - but spec section 11 requires 'The sidebar work order list virtualizes at 50+ items' and this pages instead.

19 technicians across 22 grid rows in week view with 55 blocks - above the spec's 15-technician scale. All three views switch in a comparable time with no hang: Day 2848ms/12 blocks, Week 2856ms/55, Month 2910ms/68. Scrolling and modals stayed responsive; 0 errors.
verdicts.correction: A first pass reported Month view rendering 0 blocks. That was OUR selector, not the build - Month uses .fc-daygrid-event, not .fc-timeline-event. Re-counted properly it renders 68.

verdicts.reason: Not settleable, and the reason is now firmer than 'waiting on the product owner'. The case's precondition needs a shop closure defined at shop level, and NO shop-closure, holiday or blackout concept exists anywhere in the product on this build: none of the 25 Settings tabs mentions one, and the Edit Location dialog carries no such control. So the requirement cannot be exercised even if the product owner answers. The specification still states the point two ways and the question has never been sent.

verdicts.observed: Scheduled, estimated and clocked time are three independent numbers and are free to differ. Sampling 12 shifts, 3 have all three genuinely different - S-15299 reads scheduled 720 min, estimate 1422.6 min, clocked 1302.6 min, and S-14158 reads 840 / 4064.4 / 3279.6. Nothing forces them to match: no error and no auto-correction. All three are visible to a tester in the shift modal (the TIME range gives the scheduled span, the line list gives the estimate, TIME LOGGED gives the clocked figure).

The case's own note claiming this cannot be run is FALSE - a series CAN be spread across the 1 November 2026 clock change from today, and it was. Underneath, the requirement is met: all 70 shifts of a seeded series start at 06:00 America/Edmonton on both sides, with the stored UTC correctly moving 12:00Z before to 13:00Z after. But what the case tells the tester to read - the start times on screen - moves from 12 PM to 1 PM, because the Schedule renders raw UTC rather than the shop's timezone. Proven not to be a harness artefact: the rendering is byte-identical with the browser at UTC and at America/Edmonton, and a shift stored 2026-08-05T13:00:00Z displays in the modal as '1:00 PM - 1:00 AM', which is its UTC time exactly and not its 7:00 AM Edmonton time. The workplace timezone is confirmed America/Edmonton from the API itself.

The theme control is in the profile menu ('light_mode Light  dark_mode Dark'). Switching flips body--light to body--dark and back with nothing stuck. Contrast was measured, not eyeballed: over 547 candidate elements the count of text failing a 1.6:1 luminance ratio against its nearest painted background is 0 in light AND 0 in dark, and 0 of 627 with the shift modal open. Both popovers follow the theme (Filter & Display and View Options at rgb(15,17,26) on white text) and so does the shift detail modal (rgb(32,41,57)). Conflict cues are not colour-only - the block carries a warning_amber icon and the text 'Scheduling conflict'.

verdicts.reason: The precondition is a point in time that has passed: it requires noting shifts and events BEFORE the rewrite release and comparing after. The release is long deployed and no such baseline was taken, so there is nothing to compare against. Inventing one would not be this test.

verdicts.observed: There is no Dashboard to open. The /dashboard route redirects to the work order list, and that list has no schedule or today section - its 14 columns are On Site, Status, Number, Customer, Asset, Unit, VIN/Serial #, Progress, Service Advisor, Lead Technician, Clocked In, Lines, Total Price, Created On. The 70-shift spread work order S-15875 produces no schedule row anywhere, so the one-row-per-work-order assertion has no surface to be true or false on.

There is no appointment in the work order creation flow. The New Work Order dialog offers exactly Customer, Asset, 'Asset Here?' and Save - eight controls, none of them a date or time. The work order page itself contains no appointment-like word and no appointment-like control.

Ayesha Khan AK is enrolled at BOTH locations (departments at Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and Staging Lethbridge - 4310). Her six shifts, all on Heavy-Duty work orders, appear on the Heavy Duty board; switched to Lethbridge she is not even a grid row and has zero shifts. Zero shift ids are common to the two boards. Switched back, the Heavy Duty board is identical - same 45 shifts, same id set.

No Priority anywhere. The New Work Order dialog has no Priority field; the work order list has no Priority column and the word does not appear on it; the Schedule sidebar Filters menu offers only assignment (Unassigned 27 / Assigned 64) and status (Approved 90, Estimate 0, Declined 0, In Progress 0, Ready for Review 1, Complete 0, Invoiced 0, Paid 0). The schedule work-orders payload does carry a priority key, but it is null on every one of the 91 orders and nothing sets or filters it.

verdicts.reason: The case needs three separate API sessions - no Schedule permission, View only, View+Edit - which means impersonation, and that is barred this session.

verdicts.observed: The feature has SHIPPED since it was last looked at, and all four expected results hold. A spread whose window exceeds 8 weeks WITHOUT the acknowledgement is refused HTTP 409 with 'The series would span 98 days, beyond the 56-day limit. Resubmit with acknowledgeLongSeries to schedule it anyway.' The identical request WITH acknowledgeLongSeries:true returns HTTP 201 and materialises 70 shifts under one series id (52e7be83, scheduledMinutes 4200, 2026-09-01 to 2026-12-07). A spread that would create more than 120 shifts is refused HTTP 422 'A single scheduling action may not create more than 120 shifts.' EVEN WITH the acknowledgement. The two refused calls left nothing behind - 0 stray shifts on that work order.

Item 1 PASSES and was checked exhaustively rather than sampled: a regex census for any key containing price, cost, rate, total, amount, charge, money, currency, dollar, labor, subtotal, invoice, billing, fee, discount or tax was run over the FULL response of all three endpoints. GET /api/schedule/board (132,851 bytes) and GET /api/schedule/shifts/{id} return ZERO such keys and zero dollar amounts. GET /api/schedule/work-orders (226,969 bytes) returns only totalTimeEstimateMinutes, which is minutes, and a single bare total which is the pagination row count 91. No money field of any kind, for any caller.
verdicts.not_observed: Items 2 and 3 need a caller WITHOUT Work Orders: View, which means impersonation. Not claimed.

verdicts.observed: Scoped to Lethbridge, a Heavy-Duty shift id returns HTTP 404 'Shift was not found.' on GET, on PATCH with a colour, and on DELETE. Location A's board contains only location A's shifts - zero ids in common with location B.
verdicts.disproved: A PATCH carrying only a note returned HTTP 400 'The request changes nothing.' rather than 404, which looked like an information leak. It is not. The SAME 400 comes back for a completely made-up uuid, so the guard fires before any lookup and distinguishes nothing. Comparing the foreign id against a non-existent id is what settled it, and no ticket was raised. The foreign shift was re-read afterwards and is unchanged - note null, colour #e2effe, startsAt 2026-08-03T13:00:00Z.
